lines: Use the shared operating contract first:
Inherit the shared operating contract and consume the outputs from cards `pc_0001` through `pc_0033` if they exist,
especially the environment/profile catalog, provisioning workspace, and provisioning secret policy.
Implement the HMRC Developer Hub bootstrap flow that can:
detect whether the canonical sandbox provisioning account already exists,
register it if it does not,
pause for activation or security interstitials when required,
and persist a sanitized internal workspace record for later provisioning cards.
This task is about the Developer Hub account and the internal provisioning workspace record only.
It does not yet create the sandbox application subscriptions or export credentials.
Source algorithm grounding you must honor:
- `invention_and_system_boundary.md`, especially the sections that keep HMRC sign-up and HMRC-only work outside the engine
- `security_and_runtime_hardening_contract.md` for secret, browser, and session posture.
wherever browser session / secret / controlled-boundary implications matter.
wherever account or authority context could be confused with runtime authority links.
- The provisioning workspace from `pc_0032` and secret policy from `pc_0033`.
- Current HMRC Developer Hub guidance for:
and starting from the Applications area.
- Current HMRC development practices that warn against depending on unsupported automated OAuth grant-flow web interfaces.
This task may automate Developer Hub provisioning,
but it must not be repurposed into customer runtime OAuth grant automation.
External-provider grounding you must honor at execution time:
- HMRC “Getting started” says you register for an account, activate it by email, then sign in before creating sandbox applications.
- The Developer Hub home / getting-started flow centers on `Register`, `Sign in`, and the `Applications` area.
- Sandbox tasks may remain browser-owned and copy can drift; therefore live DOM / copy revalidation is mandatory before acting.
if the account already exists, adopt it and continue;
if not, register it through the governed flow.
email verification, anti-bot checks, MFA, or suspicious-login flows must produce explicit manual-checkpoint states.
the repo-tracked record must contain aliases, environment IDs, account status, evidence refs, and console location refs,
but never raw credentials or active cookies.
- deterministic step IDs and evidence manifest binding.
1. Refresh current HMRC documentation and confirm the Developer Hub register/sign-in/applications entry points before writing selectors.
2. Create a provider-specific selector manifest that prefers role / label / text anchors and falls back to constrained URL or structural anchors only when necessary.
3. Implement the account bootstrap state machine:
- if absent, navigate to register/sign-in entry
- detect existing-account path versus registration path
- submit only the data needed by policy
- pause for email activation or security interstitials
- verify landing in the Applications area
This closes a current algorithm gap:
HMRC defines accounts and applications, but Taxat also needs one sanitized internal record that says
which controlled provisioning workspace now owns the HMRC account, for which environment, with which evidence lineage.
5. Persist only sanitized evidence and secret refs.
7. Add an optional live-run mode behind explicit environment flags and manual approval.
- Close the “there is no governed HMRC Developer Hub account bootstrap flow” gap.
- Close the “the roadmap needs an internal provisioning workspace record even though HMRC itself only exposes account/application concepts” gap.
- Close the “manual activation and security checkpoints are not yet encoded as resumable states” gap.
- Close the “later cards need a stable authenticated landing point before application registration can begin” gap.
- The account may already exist but be partially activated.
- The verification email link may expire, requiring re-trigger or human recovery.
- The portal may present cookie banners, maintenance banners, or support notices before the main flow.
- The account may already be signed in from a previous safe session; detect that instead of forcing a new login.
- Suspicious-login or MFA interstitials must not be bypassed.
- Portal copy or button text may drift; selector design must surface drift rather than misclicking.
- The run may fail after account creation but before workspace record persistence; resume must adopt the created state safely.
- Do not cross the boundary into HMRC online-services tasks unrelated to Developer Hub provisioning.
- Use Playwright for implementation and testing.
- Keep live account credentials out of source control and out of unsafe artifacts.
- Ensure manual-checkpoint persistence and resume are integrated with the workspace from `pc_0032`.
- Keep this flow isolated under the HMRC provider recipe namespace.
- The workspace record schema must be explicit about safe fields versus secret refs.
- Fixture tests must prove fresh-account and existing-account paths.
- A manual-checkpoint path must be testable without live email or live HMRC dependency.
- The flow must verify that the terminal page really is the Applications area or equivalent authoritative landing location.
- The workspace record must validate against its schema and contain no secret values.
- Live-run mode must require explicit flags and must never execute in default CI.
- A later agent can run one controlled Playwright recipe that either adopts or creates the canonical HMRC Developer Hub account,
pauses safely for human-required steps, lands in the Applications area, and leaves behind one sanitized internal workspace record

lines: - `../shared_operating_contract_0030_to_0037.md` is still absent, so the implementation grounded directly in the named algorithm contracts, the provisioning workspace from `pc_0032`, the provisioning secret policy from `pc_0033`, and current official HMRC guidance.
- Revalidated the live public HMRC Developer Hub entry points on `2026-04-18` before writing the selector manifest:
- Implemented three HMRC provider flows under `automation/provisioning/src/providers/hmrc/flows/`:
- detect-or-create workspace orchestration with sanitized record persistence

- Added one canonical selector manifest and one explicit JSON schema for the internal workspace record, then wired the orchestration so it emits only aliases, environment IDs, evidence refs, safe console refs, and vault refs.

- Added fixture-driven Playwright coverage for fresh registration, duplicate-account fallback to sign-in, activation checkpoint persistence, existing-session adoption, MFA/security interstitial handling, selector drift failure, and live-run gating.
- Fixed two non-trivial stability issues during implementation:
- page-kind detection had to preserve query parameters for fixture routes or every screen collapsed into one path
- page-state heuristics had to read visible text rather than `body.textContent`, because fixture inline script text can otherwise poison duplicate-account or checkpoint detection
